meta.description: Cross-venue settlement comparison for selected event contracts on Kalshi, Polymarket US (DCM), Polymarket International, and CME. Hand-curated from published rulebooks; not auto-refreshed.

contracts.title: Who will control the U.S. Senate after the 2026 midterms?
contracts.divergence_scenario: A contested result, recount, or legal challenge extending beyond each venue’s settlement window could force venue-specific resolution procedures. Kalshi’s Outcome Review Committee would invoke its last-traded-price provision under Rule 6.3(c); Polymarket US exercises “full discretion” under Rule 10.4. CME’s Contingency Expiration mechanism provides a defined deadline, but the determination criteria applied after that deadline are not detailed in published contract rules. Senate seating can also be delayed when special elections or certification challenges postpone the final declared majority.

kalshi.contract_title: Which party will win the U.S. Senate?
kalshi.resolution_trigger: Party holding a majority of U.S. Senate seats following the November 3, 2026 elections
kalshi.delay_revision: Not found in published rules for this contract
kalshi.ambiguity_cancellation: Rule 6.3(c): if outcome is unresolvable, settles at last-traded price prior to circumstances becoming known; Outcome Review Committee may determine a different fair settlement price if no last-traded price represents a fair settlement
kalshi.decision_path: Outcome Review Committee (ORC); “determinations of Kalshi and the Outcome Review Committee under this Rule are final and not subject to review”

contracts.title: Will there be a U.S. government shutdown at the December 2026 funding deadline?
contracts.divergence_scenario: Each venue defines “shutdown” differently. Kalshi requires an actual furlough of non-essential federal workers, explicitly excluding brief funding gaps that do not result in furloughs. Polymarket International’s nearest listed contract bundles the shutdown outcome with the House election winner, making it a fundamentally different binary. CME lists no comparable contract. A short-lived funding lapse that triggers Kalshi’s furlough definition but falls outside Polymarket’s bundled condition—or a brief gap that avoids furloughs entirely—would produce divergent settlements across every active venue. This definitional gap produced inconsistent resolution signals across venues during the January 2026 funding episode.

kalshi.resolution_source: Lapse in federal appropriations causing furlough of non-essential government employees; brief funding gaps without furloughs do not trigger resolution
kalshi.resolution_trigger: A government shutdown begins on or continues through December 12, 2026
kalshi.delay_revision: Not found in published rules for this contract
kalshi.ambiguity_cancellation: Rule 6.3(c): if outcome is unresolvable, settles at last-traded price prior to circumstances becoming known; “brief funding gaps that do not result in furloughs typically do not trigger resolution” (per market description)
kalshi.decision_path: Outcome Review Committee (ORC); determinations are final and not subject to review

polymarket_us.note: Standalone December 12 shutdown contract not confirmed in published Polymarket US listings as of 2026-09-26

contracts.title: What will the Federal Reserve decide at the October 27–28, 2026 FOMC meeting?
contracts.divergence_scenario: The Federal Reserve’s rate announcement is immediate and unambiguous; all binary event contract venues resolve against the same FOMC statement, minimizing definitional risk. The primary residual exposure is timing: if a meeting is unexpectedly postponed, Polymarket US’s Rule 10.3(b) grants the Company discretion to adjust the expiration date, while Kalshi’s ORC would make an equivalent determination, with no guarantee of identical timing. CME’s 30-Day Federal Funds Futures are a different instrument—settling against the realized monthly average rate rather than a cut/hold/hike binary—and cannot be compared directly.

kalshi.resolution_source: FOMC meeting statement / Federal Reserve federal funds rate announcement
kalshi.resolution_trigger: FOMC rate decision announced at the October 27–28, 2026 meeting
kalshi.delay_revision: Not found in published rules for this contract; general Rule 6.3(c) covers unresolvable outcomes
kalshi.ambiguity_cancellation: Rule 6.3(c): if outcome is unresolvable, settles at last-traded price prior to circumstances becoming known
kalshi.decision_path: Outcome Review Committee (ORC); determinations are final and not subject to review

cme.note: CME has no binary event contract for this FOMC meeting. CME lists 30-Day Federal Funds Futures (ticker: FF), a traditional interest rate futures contract that settles against the arithmetic average of the daily effective federal funds rate for the delivery month—not a binary cut/hold/hike outcome. Contract specs at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/stirs/30-day-federal-fund.html

case_study.title: Cardi B at Super Bowl LX (February 2026)
case_study.event: Super Bowl LX halftime show, February 2026
case_study.contract_question: Will Cardi B perform at Super Bowl LX?
case_study.description: An event contract on whether Cardi B would perform at Super Bowl LX traded on both Kalshi and Polymarket. When Cardi B made a guest appearance during the halftime show, the question of whether the appearance met the contract’s definition of a qualifying “performance” was disputed across venues.

kalshi.mechanism: Rule 6.3(c) last-traded-price settlement; outcome declared unresolvable
kalshi.notes: Kalshi determined the appearance did not clearly satisfy the contract’s resolution criteria and settled at the price at which the contract last traded

polymarket_intl.mechanism: UMA oracle resolved YES; appearance treated as a qualifying performance
polymarket_intl.notes: Resolved at full $1.00 payout for YES holders

illustrative_spread.description: 100 YES contracts held at last-traded price of $0.65 each (total cost $65.00)
